scope: Three additions and the existing BrainOmni citation in rewritten passages; existing dataset citation checks retained from prior audit. Three further additions on 2026-11-11 for the Soft-HFC practice sentence, verified at metadata and documentation level only, as each entry's basis and limits state.

entries.claim: LaBraM learns reusable EEG representations through channel patches and masked neural-code prediction.
source_locators: Section 2.1, printed pages 3-4: channel patch architecture
Section 2.3, printed page 6: masked neural-code pretraining
entries.basis: Primary conference full text and official metadata.
entries.limits: EEG method context only; no claim of OPM evaluation or superiority over BrainOmni.
entries.status_check: No correction or retraction notice found on official proceedings entry or author arXiv record; targeted title search found none. No comprehensive Crossmark check.

entries.claim: Unlike fixed cryogenic SQUID arrays, OPMs permit flexible near-scalp placement; triaxial sensors measure three orthogonal field components.
source_locators: Introduction, first paragraph: cryogenics and adaptable near-scalp placement
Introduction, triaxial discussion and Figure 1A: orthogonal components
Methods, System overview: wearable sensor array
entries.basis: Publisher full text, independently checked by hardware reviewer.
entries.limits: Does not establish our tokenizer grouping benefits, exact physical co-location, or the removed sensor-distance values.
entries.status_check: No correction or retraction notice on publisher full-text page or targeted DOI search; Crossmark not independently obtained.

entries.claim: Conventional HFC approximates distant interference as spatially homogeneous and removes its orientation-defined subspace.
source_locators: PDF page 2, Section 2.1, equations 4-7: orientation matrix and homogeneous approximation
PDF page 2, Section 2.2, equation 8: hard projection I-NN+
PDF page 3, Section 3.2: possible attenuation of neural signals
entries.basis: Published full-text PDF in institutional repository, independently checked by methods reviewer. Author list verified on PDF because repository metadata repeats authors.
entries.limits: Our inverse expression assumes full column rank. Soft-HFC and alpha=0.25 are evaluated analysis choices, not established in this source.
entries.status_check: No correction or retraction notice found in UCL/PubMed records or targeted DOI search. Publisher access blocked for reviewer; comprehensive Crossmark status not verified.

entries.claim: BrainOmni combines sensor-conditioned tokenization, residual vector quantization and masked-token learning for EEG and MEG.
source_locators: Section 2.2, Sensor Encoder, Channel Compression and Quantisation
entries.basis: Author full text read; conference metadata confirms identity. Conference PDF endpoint timed out.
entries.limits: Cited only for shared architecture. Checkpoint-specific sensor integers and mask ratio are grounded in local code, not copied from the publication. No field-wide corpus composition or sensor-distance claim remains.
entries.status_check: No correction notice visible in consulted official metadata/author version; no full renewed correction-status audit of all existing dataset references.

entries.claim: MNE-Python implements conventional homogeneous field correction, and its order argument selects the homogeneous field alone or a higher-order harmonic basis.
locations: short_paper.tex:Model, Endpoint and Interventions, Soft-HFC sentence
source_locators: compute_proj_hfc API page: order argument description and its two cited references
OPM tutorial page: compute_proj_hfc called with order=2, projectors applied with add_proj().apply_proj()
entries.basis: Official project documentation for the cited behaviour. Pages read 2026-11-11; MNE-Python is a locked dependency of this repository at 1.13.2.
entries.limits: Cited for the existence and options of the reference implementation only. We did not run it; Soft-HFC here is this repository's own partial-projection variant.
entries.status_check: Documentation page, no retraction concept. Version-dated URL not pinned; the stable URL may move with releases.

entries.claim: Interference suppression for OPM arrays has published review coverage.
locations: short_paper.tex:Model, Endpoint and Interventions, Soft-HFC sentence
source_locators: Crossref record: NeuroImage 247, 118834, 2022; title 'Interference suppression techniques for OPM-based MEG: Opportunities and challenges'
Cited as the single reference of the MNE OPM preprocessing tutorial
entries.basis: Crossref metadata and the MNE tutorial's reference list. Full text not read.
entries.limits: Used only as a pointer to a review. No result, number or recommendation from it is asserted. Promote to supported before any claim about its findings.
entries.status_check: No retraction notice seen in the Crossref record; not independently checked.

entries.claim: The homogeneous-field model generalizes to a higher-order spherical-harmonic basis for multi-axis OPMs.
locations: short_paper.tex:Model, Endpoint and Interventions, Soft-HFC sentence
source_locators: Crossref record: NeuroImage 258, 119338, 2022; title 'Spherical harmonic based noise rejection and neuronal sampling with multi-axis OPMs'
compute_proj_hfc API page: cited for the harmonic field case, order > 1
entries.basis: Crossref metadata and the MNE API page's attachment of this reference to the harmonic option. Full text not read.
entries.limits: Cited for the existence of the harmonic generalization, at the level the title and the MNE documentation state. No quantitative claim from it is asserted.
entries.status_check: No retraction notice seen in the Crossref record; not independently checked.
